correctness.rationale: Increasingness pairs the sorted domain and image uniquely. The height-two fence compares exactly adjacent distinct integers, with the direction determined by parity; hence forward and inverse preservation are precisely synchrony of the gaps of length one given pointwise parity. The square has empty domain exactly when the domain and image are disjoint. Each parity class contributes at most half its points rounded down to the rank, which forces the deficit at n=4m+2. Paired contiguous blocks of length 2m, a terminal hole at size 4m+1, an internal hole between odd blocks at size 4m+3, and restriction to the initial 4m points at size 4m+2 attain the bounds (the empty-map boundaries are correct). At saturation, gap synchrony matches ordered run-length lists. For equal numbers of each color and at most one dot, any same-color consecutive run types must straddle the sole dot and occur between whole pairs: before the repeated type the alternating prefix has even length, since after a flip at an odd prefix the two segment imbalances have the same nonzero sign. Once paired, the within-pair distance between matched points is the common run length, plus one only for an internal dot. Thus no dot gives an even composition with two orientations; a dot between pairs yields h+1 nonreversing and h-1 reversing placements for h even-length pairs; an internal dot requires the unique odd part. Summing the positive-composition counts gives 2^m, (m+1)2^m and (m+2)2^m in the stated classes.
residual_risks: Without reflection, forward fence preservation gives a different census (e.g. five rather than four top maps at n=8); that is not the frozen object. The finite enumeration is not used to infer the infinite formulas. Except n=2, exceptional-class top counts are not part of the theorem.

evidence: For part-preserving square-zero maps of a complete multipartite graph the earlier rank bound is the sum over parts of floor(part size/2), attained in that less restricted class. The unrestricted isometry theorem can instead swap equally sized parts, attaining rank 3 on K_{3,3} unlike the two-way parity fence at n=6.
The contractions result addresses maximum length k+1 of a path at rank k, not disjoint directed edges at high rank.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader part-preserving count omits the chain order and fence-neighbor synchrony, so it gives the same elementary parity upper bound but does not prove attainment in this submonoid or its exact extremal counts. The presentations and ideals do not specify the disjoint pairs.

value.rationale: Square-zero is the first nontrivial bounded-nilpotency level, and the largest possible domain at that level is a natural statistic of a submonoid with both chain and fence constraints. The residue obstruction recurs indefinitely; the exact maximum-rank multiplicities describe how the local fence rule couples otherwise independent parity packings. The one-hole classification supplies more than the parity upper bound or a small-rank census.
residual_risks: No enumeration of all square-zero strata or of the general exceptional top stratum is supplied.
